clue.text: Casino I broke in a Mediterranean capital

indicators.note: something that broke falls apart, so these letters are put back together in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler loses everything at a casino on holiday in a Mediterranean city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, an island in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Identifies northern sights on the radio

parts.note: N is short for northern

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: to sight a gun is to aim it, so sights are aims

explanation.surface: A radio presenter describes the sights of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone is to identify them by saying who they are.

clue.text: Pact made by US state capital, at last

indicators.note: placing something last puts it at the end of the word

parts.note: Concord is the capital of New Hampshire
taken as written

explanation.surface: A treaty is finally signed in an American state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: At last reads as finally, but it says to put the word at at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially one between the Vatican and a government.

clue.text: Song from a musical, "Let's Get The Show On The Road"?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Gershwin title song of a 1927 musical

definitions.text: Let's Get The Show On The Road
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a call for the musicians to begin playing

explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase looks like another song title; it is a paraphrase of the command to start the music.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for telling musicians to begin, and also the title of a famous Gershwin number.

clue.text: Answer question on amazing allure involving English watercolour painting

parts.note: A is short for answer

indicators.note: involving something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside
something amazing has been thrown into confusion, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: Q is short for question
taken as written
E is short for English

explanation.surface: Answering a question about the amazing charm of English watercolours.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarelle is a technique or picture using transparent watercolour paints, from the French word for it.

clue.text: Strong emotion shown by Oasis playing in outskirts of Preston

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside the other's letters
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the town

indicators.note: a band playing is in action, so the band's name is set moving into a new order

parts.note: the band's name taken as written

explanation.surface: Fans get emotional at an Oasis gig on the edge of Preston, a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis looks like the Britpop band in concert; it is only five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is an intense feeling such as love or anger, a synonym for a powerful emotion.

clue.text: Dish of boiled tripe

indicators.note: food that is boiled is churned about in the pot, so its letters are tumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A menu offers a plate of boiled tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: Dish looks like a plate of food; it is the shallow glass dish used in laboratories.
explanation.definitionFit: A Petri dish is a shallow lidded glass container used for growing bacterial cultures.

clue.text: Song in Groucho's bar, remarkably clean

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are set in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
a fair copy is a clean one

explanation.surface: A song is heard in a remarkably clean bar run by Groucho Marx.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarborough Fair is a traditional English ballad, made famous by Simon and Garfunkel.

clue.text: Victor letting drop wife's secret

indicators.note: letting something drop means losing it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a victor is a winner
W is short for wife

explanation.surface: A champion accidentally reveals his wife's secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Wife's looks possessive; the 's stands for is, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are private and hidden, as secret ones are.

clue.text: Gets gen confused about Society and savings

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters go round another
confused things are muddled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
S is short for society

explanation.surface: Someone gets confused information about a building society and their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Nest eggs are sums of money put aside for the future, a metaphor for savings.

clue.text: Little action in clubs, say

parts.note: minor means small or little
a suit is a legal action in court

explanation.surface: Not much going on at the nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs reads as nightclubs or golf clubs, but it is the card suit; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, clubs and diamonds are the lower-ranking pair of card suits, called the minor ones.

clue.text: Girl, a long time penning note

indicators.note: penning something means shutting it in a pen, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: ages means a very long while
N is short for note

explanation.surface: A girl takes a long time writing a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Last of Beaujolais wine in jar

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
hock is a white German wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: The dregs of a bottle of French red, left in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: Jar looks like a container for the wine, but it is the verb meaning to jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: To jar is to give a jolt or unpleasant surprise, which is what a shock does as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Pay back in rupees one in Burmese resort

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits among that other's letters
to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rupees

explanation.surface: Settling a debt in rupees at a holiday resort in Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a holiday destination; read as re-sort it tells you to shuffle the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to repay money that someone has spent or lost.

clue.text: A motoring offence within the borders of Shepperton?

definitions.text: A motoring offence within the borders of Shepperton?

parts.note: surface reading: an illegal way of leaving a car, stopped beside one already parked
setter's reading: inside the outer letters of the town name sits a pair of the same letter, P twice

explanation.surface: A traffic offence committed in the Surrey town of Shepperton.
explanation.walkthrough: Shepperton is a town near London; strip its border letters and the middle holds two Ps side by side, a doubled P making a playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a car alongside another one already at the kerb is an illegal way to stop a vehicle in Britain.

clue.text: A waste of time, like the team that always loses?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having no purpose or use

definitions.text: like the team that always loses
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a team that never wins has no points in the table

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is read literally: a team on zero has nothing in the points column.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means futile, and literally describes a side with zero points on the league table.

clue.text: Seriously trendy boy's name, reportedly

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: Ernest is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A fashionable boy's name is said in all seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun recalls Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest, built on the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in earnest means doing it sincerely and with determination, an idiom for seriously.

clue.text: Country record includes opening of "Love Song"

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it inside

parts.note: to bug a room is to record conversations secretly

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A national record includes the start of a song titled Love Song.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks make Love Song look like one title; the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a nation in south-eastern Europe on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Aware of article and short note, most recent

parts.note: being up to something can mean being aware of or engaged in it
the definite article
a minute is a brief memo or written record

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up with an article and a brief memo containing the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely current or the latest available is described with this phrase, a synonym for newest.

clue.text: Fruit's popular ammunition

parts.note: grapes are fruit; the apostrophe-s supplies the S
hot means in demand or popular

explanation.surface: A popular fruit is being used as something to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is cannon ammunition made of small iron balls packed together like a bunch of grapes.

clue.text: Love affair starts to annoy many of us

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A love affair begins to irritate a lot of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Starts to looks like the verb begins; it selects the first letters of annoy and many only.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a borrowed French word for a romance, often a secret one.

clue.text: Hospital teas prepared with speed

parts.note: H is short for hospital

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up, so the letters are made into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cups of tea are hurriedly made on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurry or quickness of action, a synonym for speed.

clue.text: Steed outside close to Gale

parts.note: hors is French for outside, as in hors d'oeuvre

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A horse standing out in the open as a gale nears.
explanation.walkthrough: Outside has to be read in French, the word familiar from hors d'oeuvre and hors de combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A steed is a literary word for a riding animal, especially a spirited one.

clue.text: Some near this planet

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the letters sit inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Something lies close to our own world.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the third planet from the Sun, the one we live on.

clue.text: Wilhelm's OK after port wine

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it in the word

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ja is German for yes, as a German called Wilhelm would say

explanation.surface: A German is happy to drink wine after the port has gone round.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the fortified wine next to another wine; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Cut eating stoned fruit, so cry

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside itself

parts.note: to shear is to cut
a date is a fruit with a single stone

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a stone fruit while eating and is moved to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoned fruit means fruit with a stone, here the date.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry is to weep, and the phrase is an idiom for letting a single tear fall from sadness.

clue.text: Shorten a card game

parts.note: taken as written
bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: Cutting a card game short.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book or text is to condense it by cutting parts out.

clue.text: Withdraw a score

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pull a horse or competitor out of a race
second meaning: a mark scored on a surface

explanation.walkthrough: A score looks like twenty or points in a match; here it is a line cut into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratch means both to drop an entrant from a contest and a thin mark gouged into something.
